dir.description:
Documentation directory

Note: This option will be automatically set

lang.description: The language of the documentation site.

name.description:
The name of the documentation site.
Defaults to the `name` of the closest `package.json` (searching upwards from the docs directory up to the repository root).

description.description:
The description of the documentation site.
Defaults to the `description` of the closest `package.json` (searching upwards from the docs directory up to the repository root).

shortDescription.description: The description of the documentation site.

url.description: The URL of the documentation site.

github.description: The GitHub repository for the documentation site.

socials.description: Social media links for the documentation site.

api.description: The URL to the sponsors JSON API.

branch.description: The branch of the GitHub repository for the documentation site.

id.description: A unique id saved to local storage to remember if the banner has been dismissed. Change this value to show the banner again.

icon.description: The icon displayed next to the title (e.g., 'i-lucide-info').

actions.description: Display a list of action buttons next to the title.

to.description: Link destination URL or route path.

oneOf.description: Display a close button to dismiss the banner.

closeIcon.description: The icon displayed in the close button (e.g., 'i-lucide-x').

ui.description: UI customization classes for banner components.

versions.description: The versions of the documentation site.

active.description: Whether the version is active on this documentation site.

themeColor.description:
The accent color of the documentation site. Defaults to `mono`.
Accepts `mono` (no accent — links and active navigation read in body color, the monochrome default), a Geist hue (`blue`, `red`, `amber`, `green`, `teal`, `purple`, `pink`), a Tailwind palette name that maps onto the nearest Geist hue (`violet` -> purple, `cyan` -> teal, `rose` -> red, ...), a neutral name (`gray`, `slate`, `zinc`, `neutral`, `stone`) as a synonym for `mono`, or any CSS color.
It tints links, active navigation, icons, and the landing glow, and is used for the `theme-color` meta tag. Buttons and other solid fills stay monochrome, as they are in Geist.

plugins.description: Undocs plugins. Each entry is a package name or `{ package, options }`. Plugins export server hooks and an optional client entry.

webmcp.description: Expose docs search/navigation to browser AI agents via WebMCP (https://webmachinelearning.github.io/webmcp/). Enabled by default — browsers without a native `document.modelContext` get a polyfill, so the tools are reachable today. Set to `false` to opt out.

redirects.description: Redirects for the documentation site, as `from: to` paths (e.g. `/docs: /guide`). A `/old/**` key redirects the whole subtree; when the target also ends with `/**`, the matched tail is preserved.

crossOriginIsolation.description:
Serve the documentation site cross-origin isolated, so pages may use `SharedArrayBuffer` and wasm threads. Off by default.
Type: `boolean | "credentialless" | "require-corp"`.
`true` (and `"credentialless"`) sends `Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin` and `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy: credentialless`, which strips credentials from cross-origin **no-cors** subresource requests so those loads need no cooperation from upstream servers. CORS fetches still require a normal CORS response.
`"require-corp"` is the stricter alternative: use it only when every cross-origin asset the docs load sends `Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy` (or CORS), since anything that does not is blocked.
Under either value a cross-origin iframe must opt into isolation — send its own `Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy`, or use the `credentialless` iframe attribute where the browser supports it — or third-party embeds (playgrounds, video) can stop loading.

landing.description: The landing page shown at `/`. `true` forces the hero on, `false` forces it off — with it off, `/` is served from the docs-root `index.md` (or `README.md`) as an ordinary page: docs layout, left sidebar, and a `Home` entry in the navigation. Any configuration here also turns it on. Left unset, it is inferred from the content: docs organised into sections get a landing, flat docs use their root page as the home page, and docs with no root page always get one (nothing else could serve `/`).

featuresLayout.description: Features section layout to be in default place or in the hero (only if there is no code)

heroDescription.description: Additional text in hero (default is same as description)

heroSubtitle.description: second hero title (default is same as shortDescription)

heroTitle.description: main title (default is same as page title)
